newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-LILLEE CALLS FOR TAYLOR TO BE DROPPED.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LILLEE CALLS FOR TAYLOR TO BE DROPPED.

text.p: Former fast bowling great Dennis Lillee has called on Australian selectors to drop captain Mark Taylor before the forthcoming Ashes tour of England.
Lillee, the highest test wicket-taker in Australian test history, said Taylor was a liability as an opening batsman because of a prolonged slump in form.
Taylor's renowned ability as a captain was insufficient reason for him to retain his place for the six-test series against England, Lillee said.
Lillee said he supported the Australian tradition of picking the best 11 players on form and then selecting a captain from within their ranks, rather than choosing a captain first.
"I don't think that you should pick a captain and then pick a team," Lillee told reporters in Brisbane.
"So if I were a selector, with all due respect, I wouldn't pick Mark Taylor because he doesn't deserve to be in as a batsman."
Taylor has not scored a half-century in his past 20 test innings. No other specialist batsman in Australian test history has kept his place while enduring such a dismal run of low scores.
Taylor's poor form prompted him to stand down as captain and opener during the current limited overs series in South Africa.
"Mark is a very good captain and a very good marshaller of men and that's terrific, but who's to say that there's not another one there," Lillee said.
Lillee, who captured 355 wickets in 70 tests, said Australia's top order had been put under increasing pressure because of Taylor's recent inability to score runs.
"We've got a lot of problems at the top at the moment, I'm not picking on anyone in particular, but the opening combination hasn't worked for a long time," he said.
Despite his loss of form as an opener, there is a strong body of opinion supporting Taylor's retention as captain based on test results this season.
Australia won a test series in South Africa to add to their victory at home against West Indies.

"It appears to be a foregone conclusion that he (Taylor) is going to be picked to go to England and I just hope that over in England on the flatter wickets he recovers and comes good, and there's a good chance he will," Lillee said.
Australia's tour squad is expected to be named next week. It will leave for England in May.
